sections.history: Tiruppanaiyur is an ancient Shaiva village near Tiruvarur, hymned in the Tevaram by Sundarar and counted among the Paadal Petra Sthalams. The village — and the temple — take their name from the panai, the palmyra, which is the sthala vriksham. The stone temple is of the Chola period; tradition holds the self-manifested lingam to have been installed by the sage Parasara, and remembers the temple as a place of refuge for a Chola prince in a time of danger.
sections.architecture: The temple follows the Dravidian plan with a gopuram, prakara and the sanctum of Soundareswarar; the goddess Soundaranayaki has her own shrine. The palmyra, the sthala vriksham, stands within the sacred precinct and gives the lord his other name, Thaalavaneswarar, lord of the palm forest. A Vinayaka shrine, tied to the refuge legend, is honoured within the complex.
sections.legends: The temple's tradition recalls the young Karikala Chola, who, in a time of danger, was secretly sent with his mother to Panaiyur by his kinsman, the Sangam poet Irumpidarthalaiyar; the queen took refuge in this temple and prayed to Vinayaka for the prince's protection. Another tradition holds that the self-manifested lingam was installed in worship by the sage Parasara. The palmyra forest that gives the village its name frames both these memories, and the lord's name Thaalavaneswarar keeps the sacred tree at the heart of the shrine.
sections.festivals: The temple keeps the Shaiva festival calendar — Maha Shivaratri, Pradosham, the Margazhi season and the annual Brahmotsavam. The Vinayaka of the refuge legend draws particular devotion, and Sundarar's hymn is cherished in the temple's tradition.
sections.experience: Tiruppanaiyur offers the pilgrim a quiet village temple shaded by the palmyra of its name, with a gentle story of a mother's prayer for her endangered son. The darshan of Soundareswarar, the self-manifested lord of the palm forest, rewards those who seek out the lesser-known Paadal Petra shrines around Tiruvarur.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Tiruppanaiyur is in Tiruvarur district, roughly 10-12 km from Tiruvarur; the nearest rail head is Tiruvarur, with local buses and taxis to the village.
